engagement.label: Engagement / nichayathartham
engagement.blurb: Dates for a nichayathartham. The rules are looser than the wedding's — the month blocks and combustion periods still apply, but the nakshatra list is wider and Saturday is not excluded.

grihapravesam.label: Griha pravesam (housewarming)
grihapravesam.blurb: Dates for entering a new home. The fixed and soft nakshatras are preferred, the growing (shukla) fortnight is preferred, and the same three months are avoided. Diaspora note: closing dates rarely bend, so the list is deliberately wider than the wedding's.

krishna_paksha.label: Waning fortnight (krishna paksha)
krishna_paksha.note: The waxing fortnight is preferred for entering a house. Families whose closing date will not move often use the waning one instead — this roughly doubles the list.

seemantham.label: Seemantham / valaikappu
seemantham.blurb: Dates for a seemantham or valaikappu. Traditionally held in the fifth, seventh or ninth month of pregnancy, so the window is fixed by the pregnancy and the family picks the best date inside it — use the month filter on the page rather than reading the whole year.

venture.label: New venture / shop opening
venture.blurb: Dates for opening a shop, office or business. The chara (movable) and kshipra (swift) nakshatras are preferred — the traditional reasoning is that a venture wants momentum, the opposite of the fixed nakshatras you want for a house.

wedding.label: Wedding muhurtham
wedding.blurb: Dates a Tamil family would normally consider for a wedding, computed at your city's sunrise. The strictest of the five lists — three whole months, both planetary combustion periods and the rikta tithis are excluded, so a thin year is a correct result, not a broken one.

pournami.label: Pournami (full moon)
pournami.note: Some families do hold a muhurtham on Pournami. Off by default because most Tamil houses avoid it.

chathurthi.label: Chathurthi (a rikta tithi)
chathurthi.note: Chathurthi is one of the rikta tithis, avoided for weddings in standard Tamil practice. Two published date lists do print weddings on it.

saturday.label: Saturday
saturday.note: Most Tamil families avoid Saturday for the muhurtham itself. A minority accept it, usually for a morning ceremony.

extra_nakshatra.label: Poosam and Thiruvonam nakshatram
extra_nakshatra.note: Two nakshatras admitted for weddings by some houses and not others. Ask your purohit before using these dates.
